success_patterns: Every passage title or snippet repeated the clue's distinctive details and one entity (Erewhon, Strom Thurmond, I Remember Mama, Winnie-the-Pooh). The agent answered with that entity directly, in the short form the passages use, with no clue words added.

Definition and glossary-style clues ('this term', 'this industrial unit is equal to...') were solved by finding the dictionary or glossary line that echoes the clue ('Apogee – The farthest point from the Earth in the Moon's orbit', 'Man-hours – an industrial unit of production equal to the work one person can produce...'). The headword being defined was the answer, given in singular dictionary form.

For 'his name was X but others called him this', the agent gave the alternate name the passages attach to the character ('Grandpa'). It did not repeat the name already in the clue or build a longer form such as 'Grandpa Walton'.

For quote, slogan or description clues ('I Like Ike', 'bear of very little brain'), the agent answered with the person or character the passages identify, using the common full name or title ('Dwight D. Eisenhower', 'Winnie-the-Pooh'), not the quoted words.

patch.reasoning: Earlier steps added many long, narrow rules and were rejected, so the patch is deliberately small. These successes show two generalizable moves that the skill does not yet state: (1) for definition or term clues, the answer is the headword of the matching dictionary or glossary line, in singular form; (2) for 'called him this' clues, the answer is the alternate name from the passages, not the name the clue already gives. Both are short additions to existing sections.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - Definition or term clues ('referred to by this term', 'this unit is equal to...'): look for the dictionary, glossary or encyclopedia line that paraphrases the clue ('Apogee: the farthest point from the Earth in the Moon's orbit'; 'Man-hours: an industrial unit equal to the work one person can do in an hour'). The headword being defined, often in a page title, is the answer. Give it in singular dictionary form ('Man-hour', 'Apogee').

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'His/her name was X, but others called him this' / 'known to most as this': the answer is the OTHER name, title or role the passages give the character ('Zeb' -> 'Grandpa'). Never repeat the name already in the clue, and do not stretch the answer with a surname or extra words ('Grandpa Walton').
